question: A 2-year-old girl presents to the emergency department with a 3-minute episode of a tonic-clonic seizure. The parents deny any previous history of seizure involving the patient or the family. Physical examination reveals an afebrile, well-groomed, and playful appearance, with normal vital signs. The patient carries a pink birthmark on the right side of her face extending from the forehead to the zygomatic arch. Which of the following findings is most likely on a head CT of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "2-year-old girl with tonic-clonic seizure" -> "possible underlying neurological condition" -> "pink birthmark on face suggests Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome associated with cortical malformations" -> "head CT likely shows prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Tonic-clonic seizure in afebrile child" -> "consider differential diagnoses" -> "pink birthmark indicates possible vascular malformation" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome is a possibility" -> "head CT may reveal calcifications" -> "most likely prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Seizure without fever" -> "evaluate for structural brain abnormalities" -> "facial birthmark suggests Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "associated with leptomeningeal angiomas" -> "head CT may show calcifications" -> "likely prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 75%

CHAIN: "Child presents with seizure" -> "no prior seizure history" -> "pink birthmark raises suspicion for Sturge-Weber syndrome" -> "Sturge-Weber syndrome can lead to calcifications" -> "head CT findings likely include prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation, including the facial birthmark (likely a nevus simplex or port-wine stain) and the seizure, raises suspicion for Sturge-Weber syndrome, which is associated with leptomeningeal angiomatosis and can lead to cortical dysplasia and seizures. On a head CT, one would expect to see calcifications, particularly in the cortical and subcortical regions, which would correspond to prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification. Therefore, the most likely finding on a head CT for this patient is prominent intraparenchymal white matter calcification.
